english.title: Publication re youth court proceedings
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being the

(A)_[proprietor of **(..SPECIFY..) newspaper,]_
(B)_[editor of **(..SPECIFY..) newspaper,]_
(C)_[publisher of **(..SPECIFY..) newspaper,]_
(D)_[body corporate providing a programme service, namely **(..SPECIFY..),]_
(E)_[person having functions in relation to the **(..SPECIFY..) programme corresponding to those of a newspaper editor,]_

(F)_[published in the newspaper]_
(G)_[included in the programme service]_

(H)_[a report]_
(I)_[a picture]_

in contravention of section 49(1) of the Children and Young Persons Act 1933.
english.legislation: Contrary to section 49(9) of the Children and Young Persons Act 1933.

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Section 49(1) indicates matters that cannot be contained in newspaper reports.

other.penalty:
A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
